newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakura buy-back unlikely soon -- analyst.
newsitem.headline: Sakura buy-back unlikely soon -- analyst.

text.p: Sakura Bank Ltd said on Tuesday that it would change its company rules to allow it to buy back up to 350 million of its shares, but analysts said it was unlikely to carry out the repurchase soon.
"While its decision to change the rules had a favourable impact on its share price today, this will probably be short-lived," said an analyst at a foreign securities company.

"It is unlikely Sakura will buy back shares anytime soon." A Sakura Bank spokesman told Reuters the bank decided to alter its corporate rules to allow for the repurchase of up to 350 million shares in order to cancel them. The plan is subject to the approval of the bank's annual shareholders' meeting on June 27.
The spokesman said the repurchase was aimed at improving the company's return-on-equity (ROE) ratio, but added that the timing had not yet been decided.
Analysts said that while repurchasing shares would help a bank increase its ROE -- a gauge of efficiency in the use of capital -- it would also cut its capital adequacy ratio.
Sakura has yet to fully dispose of its problem loans and is expected to use its shareholdings to help cut them to manageable levels in the coming year or so, analysts said.
However, to maintain its capital adequacy ratio, it was unlikely to buy back its shares soon, they said.
At the end of March, Sakura's capital adequacy ratio stood at 8.92 percent, they said.

Shizuoka Bank Ltd, a regional bank based in central Japan, also said on Tuesday that it plans to change its company regulations at a shareholders' meeting scheduled for June 27 to allow it to buy back up to 80 million of its shares.
Analysts said Shizuoka was expected to repurchase its shares in the current financial year because it was relatively unburdened by problem loans and maintained a high capital adequacy ratio.
Its capital adequacy ratio stood at 13 percent at the end of March.
The analysts said some of Japan's major nationwide commercial banks might follow the examples of Sakura and Shizuoka at their upcoming shareholders' meetings.
However, they said such moves would be unlikely to results in repurchases in the near future since many Japanese banks were still trying to cut their problem loans to manageable levels.
Sakura Bank ended the Tuesday trading session in Tokyo up nine yen at 851 while Shizuoka closed up 60 at 1310.
